newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity to sell consumer credit card business.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity to sell consumer credit card business.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said Wednesday it is talking with several potential buyers of its small consumer credit card business.
Robert Pozen, head of Fidelity's mutual fund division, said the largest players in the market are obvious candidates for the Salt Lake City-based business.
"There are four or five obvious buyers in the United States," Pozen said. "The only question is how high the premium (on the price) is."
Fidelity's consumer credit card business, launched in 1990, has 427,000 accounts covering $490 million in assets and employs 120 workers, a spokesman said.
The company is selling the business because of tremendous competition in the market and the consolidation in the consumer credit card industry, spokesman Andy Trincia said.

"We're talking with a number of potential buyers. We feel this is the right time to sell the business to realize our investment," he said. "Also, we're focusing on our investment management and brokerage business right now."
